problem: VLN training data is not representative of the distribution of test environments, so agents trained only on shortest-path style supervision generalize poorly to unseen environments.
motivation: Poor performance on unseen environments limits VLN agents. The paper argues that explicitly training the agent to explore around the initial shortest path to the target could improve generalization.
key_idea: Explore Supervision (EXPS): provide VLN agents with supervision that strategically encourages exploration in areas around the initial shortest path to the target.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so the analysis and ablations cannot be assessed. The abstract suggests that supervising exploration near the shortest path, rather than only imitating the shortest path, improves generalization to unseen environments. The reported gain is 4.77% SR on REVERIE val-unseen.
method: Explore Supervision (EXPS): a training-time supervision signal that encourages the agent to explore areas around the initial shortest path to the target.
Base model: EXPS is implemented on top of a state-of-the-art REVERIE model (not named in the abstract).
